extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: A dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task, requiring models to keep track of information in the broader discourse context rather than relying simply on local context.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Femández
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages were extracted from the Book Corpus, filtered using language models to remove easy cases, and then evaluated by human subjects through crowdsourcing to ensure the target word could be guessed from the broad context but not from the local sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), a collection of unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list. Passages were also filtered using four language models to exclude any passage whose target word had a probability >= 0.00175.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects guessed the target word in three steps: 1) one subject guessed based on the whole passage; 2) if correct, a second subject guessed based on the whole passage; 3) if correct, up to 10 subjects tried to guess based on the target sentence only (up to 3 guesses per sentence). Passages were included only if no subject in step 3 could guess the word.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A strict hit-or-miss approach was used, requiring two consecutive subjects to exactly match the missing word in the broad context, and ensuring no subject out of ten could provide it based on local context only.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 12 human annotations per item (1 for step 1, 1 for step 2, and up to 10 for step 3).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Four language models (a pre-trained RNN, a standard 4-gram model, an RNN, and a feed-forward model) were used for initial automated filtering.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely over-represented (48%), while verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are under-represented compared to the input distribution. The dataset also contains quoted direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall (71% vs 61%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Standard language models are bound to fail on it by design because the dataset was explicitly filtered to exclude passages where simple language models could predict the upcoming word.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating computational models for text understanding and broad context language modeling. The development data can be used to fine-tune models, while models should be trained on raw text from the training partition.
